title: As long as you call on Me
hook: a sacred hadith: O son of Adam, as long as you call on Me I forgive, even sins reaching the clouds
carry: as long as you call and hope, forgiven
tomorrow: forty-two hadith, start to finish. what do they look like as one life?

segments.voice: Yesterday, desires that follow: not erased, turned. Let desire follow. And the week before it: help, and be helped. Intending counts. Drawn near. Mistakes are pardoned. Just passing through. Today, the last of al-Nawawi's forty-two.
screen: `HELP, AND BE HELPED · INTENDING COUNTS · DRAWN NEAR` → `MISTAKES ARE PARDONED · JUST PASSING THROUGH · LET DESIRE FOLLOW` → `THE LAST OF THE FORTY-TWO.`

segments.voice: A missed-calls list: Mom, Mom, Mom. Some calls sit unanswered for days, and the phone still rings again. Yesterday's question: how many times can you come back before the door closes? Hadith forty-two, a sacred hadith reported by Anas, answers with no number at all. O son of Adam, as long as you call on Me and hope in Me, I will forgive you whatever you've done, and I don't mind.
screen: `MOM, MOM, MOM.` → `HOW MANY TIMES?` → `AS LONG AS YOU CALL.`

segments.voice: Three times it says, O son of Adam, and each time the picture gets bigger. As long as you call and hope: forgiven. If your sins reached the clouds of the sky, and then you asked forgiveness: forgiven. If you came with nearly an earthful of sins, and met Me without setting anything beside Me: an earthful of forgiveness. The condition isn't being clean first. It's calling, and hoping. The Qur'an says it in Pickthall's words: "Despair not of the mercy of Allah." And here's the line to tell a friend tonight: al-Nawawi's whole collection opens on intention and closes on a door that stays open. Now hold up the week. Help, and be helped. Intending counts. Drawn near. Mistakes are pardoned. Just passing through. Let desire follow. Every one of them assumes you'll fall short sometimes, and every one leaves a way back. This is the way back, said plainly.
screen: `THREE TIMES: O SON OF ADAM.` · `UP TO THE CLOUDS, AN EARTHFUL.` · `CALLING AND HOPING.` · `A DOOR THAT STAYS OPEN.` · then, large: `AS LONG AS YOU CALL.`

segments.voice: Muslims ask forgiveness with a short phrase, astaghfirullah, I ask Allah's forgiveness, often softly and many times. For the sit, say it on each out-breath, or let each out-breath carry one thing you'd like to come back from, and each in-breath the hope.
As long as you call: the last hadith of the forty-two. Calling and hoping, and a forgiveness bigger than the sky's clouds.
screen: `AS LONG AS YOU CALL — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: as long as you call and hope, forgiven. The door stays open. Forty-two of forty-two, done.

screen: `DAY 1470 COUNTS.` → `HADITH 42 OF 42 · YEAR FIVE, 44 OF 365.` → `TOMORROW: FORTY-TWO HADITH. WHAT DO THEY LOOK LIKE AS ONE LIFE?`

howItsDone: Muslims seek forgiveness with phrases like astaghfirullah, said quietly through the day and after prayer, and teachers quote this hadith to people who feel too far gone to return.

no number at all: as long as you call and hope.

fork.setup: a friend keeps breaking the same promise to God and says asking forgiveness again would be fake. what does hadith forty-two say?
options: after a few tries, stop asking; it can't be sincere anymore.
don't ask out loud; just quietly try harder next time.
as long as you call and hope, He forgives: ask again.
fork.reveal: the hadith gives no number: as long as you call on Me and hope in Me, I will forgive you, and I don't mind.

original.note: Arabic: as long as you call on Me and hope in Me. the hadith's first condition.

trapdoor: what you thought: God forgives, so it doesn't really matter.
what it means: calling and hoping keep the door open, however far you've gone.
what a scholar hears: Tirmidhi 3540, a hadith qudsi from Anas in three parts: calling, asking forgiveness, and meeting Allah without associating partners.
guess: for as long as you keep turning to Allah
only on the holy days set aside for prayer
until you have done too much to come back

chat.meaning: As long as you call on Allah and hope in Him, He forgives, even sins reaching the clouds. No number, no 'clean up first'.
